title: Sliding Stability — Shear-Friction Factor of Safety

A.description: Area of base in compression (per unit length of dam)

ΣN.description: Sum of all vertical forces (weight, vertical water components)

ΣT.description: Sum of all horizontal driving forces (hydrostatic, silt, seismic)

applicability: USBR definition. USACE uses a slightly different formulation separating pure sliding (ΣN×tanφ/ΣT) from shear-friction. Check agency-specific requirements.

FS_OT.description: Factor of safety against overturning about downstream toe

M_stabilizing.description: Moments resisting overturning (dam weight × arm, tailwater × arm)

M_overturning.description: Moments driving overturning (headwater × arm, uplift × arm, silt × arm)

title: Base Stress Distribution (Gravity Method)

σ.description: Normal stress at upstream (-) or downstream (+) face of base

applicability: Valid when resultant falls within the base (no tension or limited tension). σ_heel = ΣV/B(1 - 6e/B), σ_toe = ΣV/B(1 + 6e/B). If e > B/6, tension develops at upstream face.

title: Uplift Force — With Drains (USBR Method)
equation: U = ½γw × [Hu + Hd + (Hu - Hd)/3] × d + ½γw × [Hd + (Hu - Hd)/3 + Hd] × (B - d)
alt_form: At drain line: P_drain = Hd + (1/3)(Hu - Hd). Pressure at heel = Hu, at drain = P_drain, at toe = Hd. Trapezoidal integration.

U.description: Total uplift force per unit length

Hu.description: Headwater pressure head at heel (reservoir depth)

d.description: Distance from heel to drain line

applicability: USBR assumes drain reduces uplift to Hd + 1/3(Hu-Hd) at drain location if drains are functional. USACE may use different drain efficiency factors. If base is cracked, full reservoir pressure extends to crack tip.

title: Hydrostatic Force on Vertical Face

F_h.description: Horizontal hydrostatic force per unit length

applicability: Acts at H/3 above the base. Applied for both headwater (driving) and tailwater (stabilizing, if any).

title: Silt/Sediment Pressure (Equivalent Fluid)

F_silt.description: Horizontal force from sediment per unit length

γ_sub.description: Submerged unit weight of sediment (typically 8.5–11 kN/m³)

Ka.description: Active earth pressure coefficient = tan²(45-φ/2) (typically Ka ≈ 0.33 for φ=30°)

Hs.description: Depth of sediment at dam face

applicability: USBR commonly uses equivalent fluid weight of 3.6 kN/m³ (= γ_sub × Ka) as a simplified approach. Acts at Hs/3 above base.

title: Pseudostatic Seismic Force
equation: F_eq = α × W  (inertia of dam);  F_eq_water = (7/12) × α × γw × H²  (Westergaard hydrodynamic)
applicability: Pseudostatic method: replace earthquake with equivalent static horizontal force. Westergaard (1933) parabolic added mass approximation for hydrodynamic pressure. Modern practice uses dynamic analysis (response spectrum or time-history) for significant dams.

title: Dam Weight (Triangular Cross-Section)

W.description: Weight of dam per unit length (triangular approximation)

γc.description: Unit weight of concrete (23–24 kN/m³ conventional, 22–23 kN/m³ RCC)

applicability: Simplified triangular section. Actual section has crest width (3–6 m minimum), upstream face batter, galleries, and appurtenances.

title: Minimum Base Width (Preliminary Sizing)
applicability: Rule of thumb for preliminary sizing. B/H ratio depends on: uplift assumptions (higher uplift → wider base), seismic loading, foundation strength. Final width determined by stability analysis.

title: Temperature Rise in Mass Concrete (Adiabatic)

H_cement.description: Heat of hydration of cement (250–350 J/g for Type II)

H_pozzolan.description: Heat of hydration of pozzolan (typically 50–70% of cement)

applicability: Adiabatic = no heat loss. Actual peak temperature is lower due to heat dissipation. Typical adiabatic rise: 15–30°C for mass concrete. Control by limiting cement content, using SCMs, and pre/post-cooling.
